stairway.principle: every training block climbs like a stairway: small steps to the halfway week, slightly bigger after it, the hardest weeks last; one rule for every person
stairway.phases_by_N_note: labels only (ACCLIMATION / DRIVE / HARDEST); 12 and 8 equal generator_spec plan_types phases_by_level

placed.note: a muscle rises at most max(1 set, 7 %) a week (whole sets, helpers may add 0.5); the week total at most 7 %; 10 % is never reached

checkin.effort_10_meaning: the max I could do, and I made it (successful, 0 RIR)
checkin.couldnt_do_it: one level down or assisted next week, sets unchanged

track.note: placed sets follow the planned T(w): never more than 1 set above in week 1, never 1 or more behind (unless a schedule warning names the muscle); the week total never stays flat two weeks in a row; no "hold" without a check-in

capacity.note: the whole stairway must fit the chosen minutes: the peak week is placed first; muscles whose peak does not fit start lower (never below the floor) so every week can still climb (D-67)

group_day_reduction.note: a group whose 2 x 2 minimum on every day is above its week-1 target is trained on fewer days, each with 2 exercises

full_body_days.rule: every muscle group trained that day gets 2-4 exercises, never 1

exercises_per_group.exempt_note: conjugate four-role days stay as written (flagged, master 10.3)

long_day.note: full-body days may run a little longer (warning, not an error)

aesthetics.notes: Muscle & physique. SAME-pattern days (squat + lunge; hinge + single-leg hinge) to drive the muscle harder (COACH-ANSWER UNI-06). Knee days carry the pulls, hip days the pushes (UNI-11). v1.1: every muscle group a full-body day trains gets 2-4 exercises, never 1 (COACH-R2 R2-SES-05) - knee day: quads 3, back 2, shoulders 2 (rear delt + KB face pull, R2-LIB-04), biceps 2, calves 2; hip day: hips 3, chest 2, shoulders 2, triceps 2, calves 2. Days start short (2 sets per exercise) and lengthen as sets are added. Core opens light (2 x 2, R2-SES-03). Heavy squat Monday, heavy deadlift Friday (R2-SES-01). Session 60 min for general clients, about 90 min for bodybuilders (UNI-09). No medball except as warm-up (ATH-05). Aerobic: 4 a week (Blue, Green, Orange + a second easy Orange) + optional 20-30-min walks after workouts, adjustable by the user (COACH-R2 R2-SES-06).

athletic.pairing: cross_pattern (default) | same_pattern (high-level athletes who need more stimulus)
athletic.notes: Field / court / combat / aquatic athletes and non-competitive athletic adults and youth ('Athletic Performance', renamed from 'JUSTICE LEAGUE', ATH-13 / FIX-03; the gen-pop 'stay athletic and active' path - pickleball, tennis, golf, rec leagues - uses the non-competitive version). CROSS-pattern days by default (squat + single-leg hinge; UNI-06); SAME-pattern variant for high-level athletes who need more stimulus (UNI-06). v1.1: every muscle group a day trains gets 2-4 exercises (COACH-R2 R2-SES-05) inside the field-athlete cap of 12 exercises + the 2-exercise core block (R2-SES-04: warm-up drills never count, a superset of two small isolations counts as one). With the cross pattern that leaves room for 2 plyo/ballistic stations + 1 Olympic lift; the same-pattern variant needs fewer resistance exercises and keeps 3-4 athletic stations. Olympic work on every main day - clean days = squat days, snatch days = hinge days (R2-ATH-04). Older adults (60+): no Olympic lifts, plyos or depth jumps by default; optional with the W_OLDER_POWER warning (R2-ATH-08). Athletic patterns never count toward muscle sets (VOL-10). About 90 min competitive (max 2 h), 60 min non-competitive (UNI-09; PROPOSED). In season: 2 days, minimal bilateral (UNI-10, PER-08), game-heavy reductions (R2-ATH-07).

hybrid_crossfit.pairing: class model (one strength pattern + its UNI-11 upper group per day)
hybrid_crossfit.notes: Strength + Olympic + conditioning (CrossFit-style class, CrossFit-style bootcamp, HYROX-style fitness). Class order: warm-up -> light core block (R2-SES-03) -> skill -> Olympic/power -> strength (+ its accessories) -> WOD (OBSERVED OT18 'WARMUP/SKILL' -> 'STRENGTH/POWER' -> 'WOD'; ATH-11, ORD-03). v1.1 class model: each day trains one strength pattern and its paired upper group with 2 exercises each (R2-SES-05) plus calves on leg days; the WOD carries the conditioning. Levels (OBSERVED OT17): HALF TIME = class member (strength 3x7 -> 3x6 -> 3x5 -> 3x4 -> L5 work up to a 1RM; power 3x4 -> 3x1), FULL TIME = competitor (strength 3x7 -> 6x4; power 3x3 -> 6x3); WOD level 1-4 = 1-4 WODs a week; aerobic level 1-4 = C; C,B; C,B,A; + lactate clearance. A 1RM test only at the end of a completed block (R2-PER-07). 40-rep sets and AMRAPs live here only (VOL-11). Heavy squat and heavy deadlift on different days (R2-SES-01).

en.effort.how_hard: How heavy? Each exercise tells you how many reps to leave in the tank: "leave 2 in the tank" means you could do 2 more reps at the end of the set (about RPE 8; 3 left = RPE 7, 1 left = RPE 9). The first weeks leave more in the tank, the last weeks less. Week 1: start a little lighter, with a weight you could lift 2-3 more times.

en.effort.olympic: Olympic lifts are for power. Cleans, snatches and their dumbbell and kettlebell versions train power: move the weight as fast as you can with clean technique. Pick a weight you can move explosively on every rep; if it slows down or your technique breaks, it's too heavy. You don't need percentages for these unless you compete in Olympic weightlifting.

en.instruction.1: *Always leave 1 rep in the tank, never work up to failure but get as close as you can.
en.instruction.2: **Do steady cardio whenever you want, just don't overdo it... I recommend doing it on your aerobic days, max 40 min of steady.
en.instruction.3: ***The lower the reps, the higher the weight... Always go for 1-3 RIR (reps in reserve), aka RPE 7+.
en.instruction.4: ****When there are joint pains, usually going unilateral and/or getting away from fixed grips (barbells, bars) and going to split grips (dumbbells, kettlebells, individual grips) helps take care of some stuff.
en.instruction.5: *****If you have any questions just ask me - IG @BLAZECAMP or TWITTER @BLAZECAMP_

es.effort.circuit: constante y controlado, sin llegar al fallo
es.effort.circuit_resistance: elige un peso con el que podrías seguir moviéndote con unas 2 repeticiones de sobra al sonar la alarma
es.effort.drift: Esfuerzo planeado en la escalera: {list}. La última semana puede añadir un intensificador en un ejercicio de músculo pequeño.
es.effort.hold_quality: mantén con buena técnica, detente antes de perderla
es.effort.how_hard: ¿Cuánto peso? Cada ejercicio te dice cuántas repeticiones dejar en reserva: "deja 2 en reserva" significa que podrías hacer 2 repeticiones más al final de la serie (aproximadamente RPE 8; 3 en reserva = RPE 7, 1 en reserva = RPE 9). Las primeras semanas dejas más en reserva y las últimas, menos. Semana 1: empieza un poco más ligero, con un peso que podrías levantar 2-3 veces más.
es.effort.intensifier: última semana: se permiten intensificadores (serie MYO en el último ejercicio de máquina / aislamiento)
es.effort.max_intent: máxima intención; para cuando baje la calidad
es.effort.myo: serie MYO en la última serie
es.effort.olympic: Los levantamientos olímpicos son para la potencia. Las cargadas (cleans), las arrancadas (snatches) y sus versiones con mancuernas y kettlebells entrenan potencia: mueve el peso lo más rápido que puedas con buena técnica. Elige un peso que puedas mover de forma explosiva en cada repetición; si se frena o se rompe la técnica, es demasiado pesado. No necesitas porcentajes para estos levantamientos, a menos que compitas en halterofilia (Olympic weightlifting).
es.effort.olympic_power: muévela rápido: si la barra se frena o se rompe la técnica, está demasiado pesada
es.effort.olympic_power_db: muévela rápido: si la mancuerna se frena o la técnica se rompe, es demasiado peso
es.effort.olympic_power_kb: muévela rápido: si la kettlebell se frena o la técnica se rompe, es demasiado peso
es.effort.ten: 10 - No puedo más: lo máximo que podía hacer, y lo logré. (Si no pudiste terminar una serie, marca ese ejercicio como "No pude hacerlo".)
es.effort.wod: duro pero sostenible; mantén el movimiento limpio

es.instruction.1: *Siempre deja 1 repetición en reserva: nunca llegues al fallo, pero acércate lo más que puedas.
es.instruction.2: **Haz cardio continuo cuando quieras, solo no te excedas... Te recomiendo hacerlo en tus días aeróbicos, máximo 40 min continuos.
es.instruction.3: ***Entre menos repeticiones, más peso... Siempre busca 1-3 RIR (repeticiones en reserva), es decir RPE 7+.
es.instruction.4: ****Cuando hay dolor articular, normalmente ir a trabajo unilateral y/o dejar los agarres fijos (barras) y usar agarres separados (mancuernas, kettlebells, agarres individuales) ayuda a resolver algunas cosas.
es.instruction.5: *****Si tienes alguna pregunta, solo pregúntame - IG @BLAZECAMP o TWITTER @BLAZECAMP_

es.why.preference: Coincide con tu preferencia de equipo

es.why.r3_pending: Valor por defecto pendiente de confirmación del coach ({id})
es.why.rear_delt_own: Los deltoides posteriores tienen sus propias series
es.why.rep_cap: Este ejercicio tiene su propio límite de repeticiones
es.why.reps_matrix: Rango de reps para este tipo de ejercicio y tu objetivo

es.why.rest: Descanso para este tipo de trabajo

es.why.second_exposure: Ejercicio distinto de la misma categoría en la segunda exposición
es.why.set_added: Serie añadida al primer ejercicio del músculo

es.why.stairway_step: Paso planificado esta semana: {pct}% ({part} de la escalera)

es.why.superset_short: Superserie para ajustarse a la duración
es.why.taper: Puesta a punto antes del primer partido
